summary: Completed a catalogue-wide link-audit pass: all 211 other raw-atlas roadmaps and six additional blueprint roadmaps were screened, with detailed source/use checks for the retained interfaces. Four existing RootSystems/UniversalCovers arrows are reused rather than duplicated. Fourteen new links and eleven scope/ownership proposals separate real differentiation/integration from algebraic, p-adic and infinite-dimensional analogues. Comparison requests and source-statement corrections remain explicit; complete refers to this link-audit pass, not implementation or mathematical closure of the LieGroups roadmap.

provenance.snapshotVerification: GitHub compare shows one intervening presentation/classification commit and no changes to atlas, roadmap documents, baseline, protocols, or link packets. The deployed snapshot is used as a read-only local input; only the two authorised deliverables are submitted.
provenance.libraryAssessment: No Lean declaration existence or absence is asserted. Declaration names inside quotations are roadmap promises. No Lean code was added or compiled.
provenance.confidencePolicy: Explicit only when the roadmap text names the other roadmap; otherwise inferred from a checked output/use pair. Hypothesis restrictions and remaining comparison work are stated in the reason.
provenance.refreshVerification: Atlas, baseline and check_links.py byte-identical to the 262dee3 snapshot. Added link packets and roadmap definitions from the be09b0f Pages artifact were loaded for validation and duplicate screening.
provenance.coveragePolicy: Every raw-atlas summary was read. All readmes and stage descriptions were searched for finite-dimensional Lie-group terms, with candidate-stage passages opened. Summary-only entries are labelled as such; none means no retained source/use pair, not proved absence. The six additional definitions were screened at summary/purpose/stage-inventory level.

links.reason: Use the arbitrary characteristic-zero Ado theorem with K=R to embed a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra in endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional real space. Choosing a basis gives the matrix Lie algebra used by the Frobenius construction. The strengthened nilpotence theorem and the positive-characteristic track are not prerequisites. Ado’s Levi argument consumes algebraic Casimir-based Weyl reducibility, not compact integration; retain that route to avoid a cycle. The cover construction must be an independent early prefix of LieGroups Layer 5.

evidence.quote: Since `ker(ad) = Z(L)`, the direct sum `ρ₀ ⊕ ad` is faithful.
Prove it via the real specialization of the [**Ado–Iwasawa theorem**](../AdoIwasawa/README.md)

links.reason: Import the general-field PBW filtration and normalized ordered-monomial basis, specialized to R and its complex scalar extension. Do not duplicate PBW in the geometric differential-operator construction or import semisimplicity into arbitrary Lie groups. LieGroups still proves that its differential-operator representation is an isomorphism, including the order/symbol comparison; the universal property alone supplies only a homomorphism.

evidence.quote: the PBW filtration; its multiplicativity and the associated-graded equivalence with the symmetric algebra `Sym(L)`
The **PBW theorem** and the PBW basis are [../LieHighestWeight](../LieHighestWeight/README.md)'s targets

links.reason: The finite-dimensional irreducible highest-weight classification identifies the geometric section representation after LieGroups proves the Borel–Weil construction and its highest-weight property. Restrict to characters of the chosen group’s Borel, not all weights of a simply connected covering algebra. For a reductive group, the semisimple classification also needs the separately specified central character; holomorphic integration and central-kernel descent are consumer obligations.

evidence.quote: `λ ↦ L(λ)` is a bijection from **dominant integral weights** to isomorphism classes of **finite-dimensional irreducible** `L`-modules
the **irreducible** `L(λ)` of [../LieHighestWeight](../LieHighestWeight/README.md) (`irreducibleQuotient`)

links.reason: Use the same finite nonzero normalized Haar probability on the compact connected G and its compact torus T, with the specified invariance and uniqueness. The |W| factor and root density belong to the Weyl integration proof, not to Haar normalization. CompactGroups Layer 0 is valid for general compact groups and does not depend on maximal tori or complexification.

evidence.quote: `haarProb_apply_univ : haarProb G univ = 1` and `isProbabilityMeasure_haarProb`
with maximal torus `T` and normalized Haar `μ_G`, `μ_T`

links.reason: The shared manifold inverse-function theorem supplies the local-diffeomorphism conclusion once LieGroups has proved smoothness and the derivative identity for its own exponential. Apply its boundaryless finite-dimensional real specialization; do not import geodesic completeness or identify the Lie exponential with the Riemannian exponential. The generic inverse-function prefix must be independently usable before Hopf–Rinow’s geodesic summit.

evidence.quote: for `C¹` boundaryless Banach manifolds, a `C¹` map whose `mfderiv` at a point is a continuous linear equivalence induces a `LocalDiffeomorphAt` there.
so (inverse function theorem) `lieExp` is a **local diffeomorphism at `0`**

links.reason: Specialize the differential-of-conjugation/adjoint identity to the smooth real Clifford-unit group and Spin subgroup. SpinRepresentations owns the bivector-to-skew-adjoint identification and the scalar fixed by its polar-form convention. For the complex version prove complex-linearity after the underlying-real comparison; this is not a theorem for Clifford algebras over arbitrary fields.

evidence.quote: The milestone is that it is the derivative of `Ad`: `ad = d(Ad)_1`
state the compatibility `d(conjugation) = ad(bivector)` as a named lemma

links.reason: The Lie functor turns the smooth spin covering homomorphism into the Lie homomorphism to be compared with the explicitly constructed bivectors. Spin must provide smooth group structures, smoothness/local-covering facts and the complex-linear comparison where required. The purely algebraic Clifford and abstract double-cover constructions remain independent of this analytic compatibility theorem.

evidence.quote: For a smooth homomorphism `φ : G →* G'`, `lieMap φ = d(φ)_1 : 𝔤 →ₗ⁅ℝ⁆ 𝔤'` is a **Lie-algebra homomorphism**
The Lie-algebra homomorphism differentiating `spinToSpecialOrthogonal` is the isomorphism `soEquivBivector` composed with the adjoint action

links.reason: Differentiation and functoriality supply the compatibility between the compact group action and the infinitesimal action in a (g,K)-module. Apply them to finite-dimensional K-stable pieces, then pass to the locally finite union and complexify the real Lie algebra. Infinite-dimensional Frechet differentiation/globalization is additional AF.1 analysis and is not supplied by this finite-dimensional Lie functor.

evidence.quote: Functoriality: `lieMap (id) = id`, `lieMap (ψ ∘ φ) = lieMap ψ ∘ lieMap φ`.
Define compatible (g,K)-modules with algebraic infinitesimal action, locally finite K action and derivative compatibility.

links.reason: The identification of the real enveloping algebra with left-invariant differential operators, followed by complex scalar extension, is the algebraic operator interface used by archimedean differentiation and uniform moderate growth. AF.0 still proves continuity, seminorm/growth bounds and the right-translation convention (including any opposite-algebra/sign conversion). Finite-place locally constant operators do not come from this real Lie theorem.

evidence.quote: `UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra ℝ 𝔤` (Mathlib) is the algebra of **left-invariant differential operators** on `G`
Define uniform moderate growth for all differential operators

links.reason: For real reductive points in a class admitting the stated global Cartan decomposition, quotienting the K times p diffeomorphism identifies G/K with p and supplies its contraction and homogeneous smooth structure. ALS.0 retains the reductive-center correction, finite component data, arithmetic stabilizers and neatness; these are not consequences of the Cartan theorem. A reductive Lie algebra alone is not an adequate group hypothesis.

evidence.quote: the map `K × 𝔭 → G`, `(k, X) ↦ k · lieExp X` is a **diffeomorphism**
Construct Cartan involutions, maximal compact subgroups and the contractible symmetric space with G(F∞)-action.

links.reason: The compact-real-form existence interface is needed to define the Cartan involution in the Hermitian-domain construction. Use the complexification of the relevant algebraic real group with a proved analytic comparison, not the incorrect blanket assertion that a noncompact real group is itself maximal compact. ShimuraData owns the positivity criterion, stabilizer, Hodge tangent decomposition and integrability; no classification of all real forms is imposed.

evidence.quote: State the compact-real-form existence as a milestone.
Define a Cartan involution using the compact real form of the complexified group.

links.reason: The reductive extension supplies the missing central-character factor when the group in Borel–Weil is reductive rather than semisimple. Restrict to the one-dimensional central characters that integrate to the chosen group torus and descend through its central quotient. This is a classification of irreducibles, not a claim that every module of a reductive Lie algebra is semisimple.

evidence.quote: Together these classify the irreducibles as (derived-ideal irreducible) × (central weight).
For a complex reductive `G_ℂ` with maximal torus `T_ℂ`

links.reason: The independent universal-cover prefix supplies the smooth simply connected covering group of SL2(R), needed for the SL2-tilde model geometry. GeometricTopology still constructs the homogeneous Riemannian metric, the actual maximal isometry group and the comparison with its model carrier. Neither the universal cover alone nor Lie III proves the JSJ or geometrization theorem.

evidence.quote: Every **connected** Lie group `G` has a **universal cover** `G̃` that is a simply-connected Lie group with a **covering homomorphism**
`S³`, `E³`, `ℍ³`, `S² × ℝ`, `ℍ² × ℝ`, `SL₂~`, `Nil`, `Sol`, each with its maximal isometry group

links.reason: Use the general constant-rank smooth Frobenius prerequisite named in LieGroups Layer 4, not its later Lie III conclusion, to identify bracket-involutive subbundles with local foliation charts. GeometricTopology owns maximal leaf assembly, tautness, plane-bundle orientations and the Euler class. The shared theorem must be built for arbitrary finite-dimensional smooth manifolds, not only left-invariant distributions on a Lie group.

evidence.quote: State the Frobenius theorem (`VectorField.mlieBracket`-involutive ⇒ integrable) as the named analytic prerequisite.
A **foliation** of `M` as an integrable subbundle of `TM` (a distribution closed under Lie bracket), equivalently a maximal atlas of flat charts

overlaps.detail: Both exponential constructions require parameter-dependent local flows and an inverse-function theorem, but a geodesic spray and a left-invariant vector field are different vector fields, and their exponential maps need not agree.
overlaps.proposal: Keep the boundaryless-manifold inverse-function prefix in HopfRinow’s shared manifold API. Extract local existence, uniqueness and smooth parameter dependence for arbitrary smooth finite-dimensional vector fields there, with domain and time restrictions explicit. LieGroups owns the one-parameter subgroup law and global completeness of left-invariant fields; HopfRinow owns its geodesic spray and metric/geodesic completeness. Do not make either global-completeness theorem a prerequisite for the other. The Frobenius prefix needs the arbitrary-vector-field version and must not wait for Ado or Lie III.

overlaps.detail: The generic compact-group Peter–Weyl/Schur theory and LieGroups’ torus/complexification theory meet at compact Lie groups, but generic Peter–Weyl neither assumes a Lie structure nor requires a complexification. LieGroups’ introductory claim that complexification feeds Peter–Weyl must not become a reverse foundational dependency.
overlaps.proposal: Keep CompactGroups responsible for compact Hausdorff harmonic analysis, convolution, finite-dimensional coefficient spaces and completeness without Lie assumptions. LieGroups owns maximal tori, the Weyl density and complexification. Put finite-dimensional Lie-group highest-weight identification after the independent compact decomposition. The by-hand SU2 example may compare with the general Weyl formula but does not make general character orthogonality depend on it.

overlaps.detail: Both expose enveloping algebras and central characters. Algebraic PBW supplies a basis and filtration, not automatically the geometric differential-operator isomorphism. LieGroups’ assertion that the centre acts by scalars needs a representation hypothesis: over R a one-dimensional abelian algebra can act irreducibly by rotation on R2 without acting by real scalars, as the reductive-algebra roadmap already records.
overlaps.proposal: Keep PBW and normalized monomials in LieHighestWeight. LieGroups owns the map to left-invariant differential operators, the symbol/filtration comparison and its inverse. State scalar central action for finite-dimensional complex irreducibles (or an explicitly supplied infinitesimal character), not arbitrary real irreducibles. Separate algebraic central weights from the integral group characters that survive integration and central-kernel descent.

overlaps.detail: ClassicalGroups’ diagonal algebraic torus in GL_n(C) and LieGroups’ compact maximal torus are not the same group. A Lie-algebra central weight is not automatically an algebraic or compact-torus character. The disconnected orthogonal group also cannot be classified from its Lie algebra alone.
overlaps.proposal: Keep rational classical-group representations and their integer character lattices in ClassicalGroups. LieGroups supplies compact real forms, compact maximal tori and differentiation/integration after the relevant smooth structures exist. Add an explicit comparison between (S1)^n and (C*)^n, their character lattices, and the chosen central quotient; transport the highest-weight parametrization through that comparison. Handle O_n/SO_n component extension separately.

overlaps.detail: Closed subgroup schemes, fppf quotients and algebraic Bruhat decompositions are different objects from smooth real closed subgroups and complex-analytic homogeneous spaces. Neither an arbitrary fppf quotient nor a positive-characteristic group follows from Cartan’s real closed-subgroup theorem.
overlaps.proposal: Keep Hopf ideals, quotient representability, scheme-theoretic Borels/parabolics and algebraic Bruhat cells in ReductiveGroups. LieGroups owns smooth subgroup charts and the analytic quotient/flag-manifold theory. Request a characteristic-zero analytification comparison for the chosen smooth algebraic G, H, B and P, with representability and compatible quotient maps proved. Do not add an unconditional dependency between the entire two subgroup stages.

overlaps.detail: LieGroups Layer 8 constructs full flags G_C/B and line bundles for Borel characters. ShimuraData D3 needs a parabolic compact dual G/P, the Borel embedding, horizontal geometry and descent to the reflex field. A full-flag theorem alone supplies neither that partial flag nor its algebraic descent. AutomorphicBundles B0 additionally needs associated bundles for general parabolic representations, not only character line bundles.
overlaps.proposal: Add a LieGroups-owned partial-flag analytic unit with P closed complex parabolic, the projection G/B to G/P, tangent quotient and complex structure. Compare it with the algebraic homogeneous variety supplied by ReductiveGroups. ShimuraData owns the Hodge cocharacter parabolic, open-domain/Borel embedding, horizontality and reflex-field descent. Keep the character/sign conventions of Borel–Weil separate from the reflex-field field-of-definition statement. Keep the generic torsor-associated-bundle functor in ReductiveGroupsPartII as B0 explicitly requests, and the analytic/arithmetic coefficient-descent comparison in AutomorphicBundles.

overlaps.detail: Both stages use the names Cartan and Iwasawa decomposition, but LieGroups concerns real reductive groups, real smooth spaces and K times p; RG2.4 concerns nonarchimedean points, special maximal compact subgroups and dominant coweights/buildings. Equal theorem names do not give an applicable prerequisite.
overlaps.proposal: Keep the real-analytic and nonarchimedean decompositions separate. Share only an explicitly compared root/weight combinatorial interface when its hypotheses match; root valuation data and the special maximal compact subgroup remain in ReductiveGroupsPartII. No LieGroups9 to RG2.4 arrow is asserted.

overlaps.detail: Layer 7 allows a noncompact real reductive G and then says it embeds as a maximal compact subgroup of its complexification. That conclusion is incompatible with the word noncompact. ShimuraData only needs the valid compact-real-form and Cartan-involution interface.
overlaps.proposal: Split Layer 7 into compact connected G with a complexification and maximal-compact embedding, and a separate real-form discussion for noncompact reductive groups with the correct global group hypotheses. State the universal property for continuous source homomorphisms and holomorphic target homomorphisms. Supply central-quotient and chosen-real-form comparisons before applying it to ShimuraData; do not repair the statement by silently deleting the noncompact case.

overlaps.detail: Local BCH and existence of a simply connected integrating group do not yet supply the global nilpotent exponential coordinates and rational/filtered lattice data needed for nilmanifold and nilsequence complexity.
overlaps.proposal: Create an early LieGroups nilpotent unit: finite-dimensional real nilpotent Lie algebra, finite BCH polynomial, its global group law, and the exponential diffeomorphism for the connected simply connected nilpotent group. Keep rational Malcev bases, lattice/cocompactness criteria, filtrations, coordinate-height and quantitative complexity bounds in AdditiveCombinatorics. Its inverse theorem and corrected nilsequence argument still require their own source proofs. Do not treat local BCH as an already-complete global quantitative supplier.

overlaps.detail: A compact real form of a complex group is not by itself the compact dual of a specified symmetric pair. BorelRegulators R.3 needs the classical compact homogeneous spaces and fibrations, while R.2 already imports continuous/relative cochains through AF.1a.
overlaps.proposal: LieGroups should expose a Cartan-involution-compatible compact-dual pair, with the k plus i p Lie algebra and actual groups/subgroups, central quotient and homogeneous manifold comparison. BorelRegulators owns the classical compact-dual cohomology, primitive generators, stabilization maps and stable-range arithmetic estimates. Reuse AF.1a for invariant forms and van Est, and AlgebraicTopology for bundle/fibration comparison; do not make the rank theorem a prerequisite for this geometric prefix.

overlaps.detail: A closed embedded Lie subgroup theorem is not the smooth homogeneous-quotient theorem. Compact maximal-torus arguments, flags, symmetric spaces, homogeneous dynamics and nilmanifolds all need compatible quotient carriers; an immersed nonclosed subgroup cannot be substituted.
overlaps.proposal: Assign an early LieGroups homogeneous-quotient unit for closed H: Hausdorff smooth G/H, quotient submersion, local sections/principal H-bundle, tangent space g/h at the identity coset and action/normal-subgroup comparisons. A Lie group structure on G/H requires normal H. A discrete subgroup acts freely on G by translations even when it has torsion; arithmetic actions on G/K instead need their separate stabilizer/freeness hypotheses. Keep finite volume, measures, ergodic/mixing/nondivergence estimates and quantitative lattice results with the arithmetic consumers.
